risks.title: PA oscillation or spurious output above simulation at 146 MHz

statement.condition: the 5 W PA (TX) is verified before fabrication only by LTspice simulation with vendor or fitted device models whose accuracy at 144 to 148 MHz and 5 W output has not been confirmed by measurement, the owner's bench has no oscilloscope (SI-013), and the tinySA Ultra spectrum analyzer the owner committed to buy (SI-034) is not yet in hand or characterized (SI-003, SI-010)
statement.departure: the built PA oscillating, or producing harmonic and spurious levels higher than simulated
statement.asset: the TX subsystem (PA stage and output low-pass filter) and the 47 CFR 97.307 emission requirements allocated to it
statement.consequence: first-power-on failure of the transmitter, a second board spin (USD 300 to 800, 6 to 12 weeks), and a possible emission-limit exceedance that the bench cannot detect until the analyzer and its attenuator are characterized (RSK-011)

risks.likelihood_rationale: Single simulation chain (LTspice) with device models not validated against measured data at VHF and no prototype stage before the turnkey build. Anchor level 3: an analysis will exist but model fidelity is unconfirmed.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimensions first_power_on, cost, schedule, performance_margin and safety all at 4: an unstable PA means the core TX function does not work and a second fabrication plus assembly run is needed; a spurious level above the 97.307(e) limit is a regulatory requirement miss (regulatory rule of process section 7); harmful interference to a safety-of-life or other service is the Critical severity of HZ-008, which maps to register safety 4 (hazard link rule, process section 1). PA self-heating itself is bounded by the supply current limit and the thermal response of the safety manager (RSK-006). An output-power shortfall of a stable PA is RSK-027.
risks.source: Formulation risk identification 2026-09-25 against SI-003, SI-010, SI-013; condition updated the same day for SI-034; SRR research candidate pass 2026-09-25 merged REFDES-7, PADEV-10, PADEV-13, PATK-10, PATK-12, RF-1; SRR ADR candidate pass 2026-09-25 merged ADR012-R1

Run a small-signal stability analysis (Rollett K and mu factors) of the PA from 1 MHz to 1 GHz in LTspice with results exported and checked by a Python pass/fail script; require K > 1.2 and mu > 1.1 at every frequency with nominal, +10 % and -10 % passive tolerances.

risks.title: LO frequency error exceeds the 500 Hz CW filter half-bandwidth

statement.condition: the receiver selectivity is a 500 Hz CW filter and the transmit and receive frequencies derive from a TCXO reference through the synthesizer chosen by cost and performance trade (SI-029, ADR-013); a typical +/-2.5 ppm TCXO alone corresponds to +/-365 Hz at 146 MHz before aging and temperature drift, and each of two cwht units (SI-019) carries its own error
statement.departure: the net frequency offset between two cwht units, or between a cwht and another station, exceeding the filter half-bandwidth of 250 Hz
statement.asset: the RX subsystem (CW filter and LO) and the stakeholder expectation of tuning to a frequency and chatting (SI-005)
statement.consequence: the other station's signal falling outside the passband, inaudible or badly detuned, so that operators cannot find each other without a search procedure

risks.likelihood_rationale: A +/-2.5 ppm reference alone consumes more than the filter half-bandwidth; without a tighter reference, receiver incremental tuning or a wider filter the departure is likely. Anchor level 4: no frequency error budget exists yet.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension performance_margin 4: the stakeholder expectation SI-005 (tune and chat) is not met as stated, although contacts remain possible by searching, so the MOE is degraded rather than lost. first_power_on 3: the radio works but a core use case is degraded until a firmware or filter change. Cost 2: a tighter TCXO grade is a USD 25 to 100 BOM delta over the build quantity.
risks.source: Formulation risk identification 2026-09-25 against SI-004, SI-005, SI-019

steps.action: Write the frequency error budget: TCXO initial tolerance, aging per year, temperature coefficient over 0 to 40 C, synthesizer resolution, filter center-frequency tolerance; state the worst-case two-unit offset and the offset after a single-point calibration.

Trade study of reference grade (0.5 ppm versus 2.5 ppm TCXO), filter bandwidth (500 Hz fixed versus 500 Hz and 1 kHz selectable) and receiver incremental tuning, scored with the register scales (process section 13).

Derive SW requirements for receiver incremental tuning, a tuning step of 50 Hz or finer, and a stored frequency calibration constant settable from the menu (frequency control is mission-critical per charter section 10).
Write the calibration procedure for the operations handbook: zero-beat against a signal of known frequency (a local repeater output or an already calibrated unit) and store the constant.
Analyze the CW filter center-frequency tolerance with a Monte Carlo over component tolerances and include it in the budget.

triggers.condition: Frequency budget worst-case error after calibration exceeds 100 Hz (40 % of the filter half-bandwidth)
triggers.response: Claude changes the TCXO grade or widens the filter and re-runs the budget before CDR; a CR is opened if a baselined requirement changes

triggers.condition: The selected TCXO has no distributor stock at PDR
triggers.response: Apply the RSK-005 alternate-part procedure the same session

mitigation.fallback: Widen the CW filter to 1 kHz nominal (CR against the selectivity requirement) and rely on receiver incremental tuning; contacts remain possible with reduced propagation advantage (SI-004).

risks.closure_criteria: Frequency accuracy requirement verified on two delivered units by a zero-beat test with a measured offset of 100 Hz or less after calibration.

statement.condition: Emulation is the optional, secondary pre-power-on evidence class for whole-binary scenarios (event ordering only, never timing; charter section 9, SI-026, ADR-011), implemented on rp2350-emu, a personal research project with no maintenance commitment (07 section 12), and no per-peripheral accreditation against the Pico 2 development board has been performed yet
statement.departure: an emulation scenario passing while the real RP2350 orders events or exposes peripheral register semantics differently, or the emulator failing to boot the release image so that Emulation evidence is unavailable
statement.asset: the SW subsystem (keyer, transmit sequencing, safety manager, charging supervision) and the first-power-on objective SI-010
statement.consequence: a firmware ordering fault discovered only on the assembled board, unit damage if the fault is in PA enable or charging sequencing, and loss of the Emulation evidence class for the affected requirements

risks.likelihood_rationale: rp2350-emu models a subset of peripherals and has no accreditation record; PIO and precise timer behavior are the least likely to be faithful, and a boot failure of a bare-metal rustos image is plausible. Anchor level 4: no fidelity assessment exists.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimensions first_power_on and schedule at 3: with HostUnit as the primary evidence (SI-026) and dev-board checks available, an emulator escape degrades one subsystem, is fixed by a USB reflash, and costs 3 to 6 weeks of root-causing without an oscilloscope. Safety 2: hardware interlocks and the safe-state manager (charter section 10, SWE-134) bound the damage from a mis-sequenced PA enable or charger.
risks.source: Formulation risk identification 2026-09-25 against SI-007, SI-010; re-scoped the same day to the secondary evidence class of charter section 9 (SI-026); listed in 07 section 21 as 'Emulator fidelity'; SRR research candidate pass 2026-09-25 merged EMUACC-R1, EMUACC-R2, EMUACC-R3, EMUACC-R4, EMUOPT-R1, EMUOPT-R2, EMUOPT-R3; plan candidate SEP21-EMU (SRR plan-table pass 2026-09-25)

statement.condition: the PA dissipates on the order of 4 to 7 W of heat at 5 W RF output (40 to 55 % efficiency) inside a pocket-sized aluminum enclosure designed in OpenSCAD and CNC-machined by PCBWay (SI-001, SI-008, ADR-008); heat must flow from the device thermal pad through PCB vias and a mechanical interface to the enclosure wall, and no thermal instrument beyond a multimeter thermocouple is available (SI-013)
statement.departure: the PA junction temperature exceeding the device rating during sustained CW keying
statement.asset: the TX subsystem (PA device) and the sustained 5 W operating scenario
statement.consequence: PA derating or thermal shutdown during contacts, and shortened device life or failure of the PA

risks.likelihood_rationale: Several watts in a pocket enclosure is a tight thermal design; no thermal budget exists yet and the PCB-to-enclosure interface is undefined. Anchor level 3.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension performance_margin 4: sustained 5 W output (SI-003, a key driving expectation) is not met if the PA must fold back. statement.consequence: units that fail the selectivity or MDS requirements, a rework of SMD crystals the owner cannot do (SI-031), or a CR relaxing the TBR set

risks.source: SRR research candidate pass 2026-09-25: candidates CWSEL-6 and CWSEL-11 (docs/research/cw-selectivity-options.md implications 6 and 11) and REFDES-10 (docs/research/2m-cw-transceiver-reference-designs.md implication 10) entered as one family

statement.condition: 07 section 16.2 row 'Keying and control inputs' assesses command injection through the key and paddle jack, the encoder and the buttons at L1, C4; charter section 12 scopes the SWE-154 tailoring to USB firmware loading and command injection via the key input; on the key line, REQ-SW-KEYER-020 (debounce), REQ-SW-KEYER-024 (key-input mode change by menu only) and REQ-SW-KEYER-028 (keying sources) and the HostUnit case TC-SW-KEYER-040 (flood, sub-filter glitches and crafted patterns change no keyer setting) exist at Draft; no requirement or case yet covers the configuration fields outside the keyer (frequency, power step, TX-arm default) or the encoder and button inputs
statement.departure: a crafted signal sequence on the key, paddle, encoder or button inputs changing the radio's configuration or operating state other than through the operator's intended keying and menu actions
statement.asset: SW-KEYER, the control input path (CTL) and the licensee's regulatory compliance (SI-014)
statement.consequence: a changed frequency, power or TX-arm setting that could produce an emission outside the 47 CFR 97.305 or 97.307 limits without the operator knowing (unintended or held keying is carried by RSK-024)

risks.likelihood_rationale: Band argument (06 section 6 case (c), a threat risk): the attacker needs physical access to the jack or the controls and a crafted sequence, and gains nothing that a person holding the unit could not do with the controls; 07 section 16.2 assesses L1. Level 1 (below 5 %), confidence Medium, until S1 and S2 are verified.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension performance_margin 4 by the regulatory rule of 06 section 7 (a changed frequency or power could breach 47 CFR 97.305 or 97.307); 07 section 16.2 scored C4. Safety 2: the hardware PA-enable cutoff (HZ-004 K5) bounds a carrier.
risks.source: 07 section 16.2 row 'Keying and control inputs' (plan candidate SEP16-KEY); charter section 12 cybersecurity row (command injection via the key input); opened 2026-09-25 after INSP-007 finding F-03

steps.action: Write the firmware-wide SW requirement that no sequence on the key, paddle, encoder or button inputs outside the menu's confirmed commands changes any configuration field (frequency, power step, TX-arm default, keyer settings; CS-30), with its cyber tag.

Extend the HostUnit injection cases from the key line (TC-SW-KEYER-040) to the encoder and button inputs and to every configuration field of S1: floods, glitches, crafted sequences and stuck inputs change no setting (07 section 16.4).
Re-run the 07 section 16.2 assessment of the keying and control inputs against the PDR architecture and the CDR design (RMM SWE-156 residual).

triggers.condition: A design change lets a key, paddle, encoder or button sequence outside the menu change configuration (for example a key-line shortcut)
triggers.response: Claude re-assesses this risk the same session and adds the sequence to the S2 injection cases before the change is approved

triggers.condition: An S2 injection case fails
triggers.response: Claude opens an NCR the same session and blocks the release until the case passes

mitigation.fallback: Remove every configuration path reachable from the key inputs; configuration changes only through the menu with two independent actions (SWE-134 d).

risks.closure_criteria: TC-SW-KEYER-040 and the S2 cases passing on a credited HostUnit run against the S1 requirement and the keyer requirements, and the 07 section 16.2 CDR re-assessment recording no input path to configuration outside the menu.

risks.title: Command injected on the diagnostic interface changes configuration

statement.condition: 07 section 16.2 row 'Diagnostic interface' assesses command injection at L1, C2 on the UART header (or USB CDC if the PDR ADR selects it) used to read the event log; the protocol is planned read-only except reboot (CS-33) and the interface is not populated on delivered units unless the owner requests it; the TC-SW-DIAG injection cases of 07 section 16.4 are not written and the diagnostic-interface ADR is due at PDR
statement.departure: a command sent on the diagnostic interface changing configuration, calibration or radio state beyond the permitted reboot
statement.asset: SW-DIAG and the configuration and calibration of a delivered unit
statement.consequence: a unit whose settings were changed without the operator's action, up to a calibration or frequency setting that could produce an emission outside the 47 CFR 97.307 limits

risks.likelihood_rationale: Band argument (06 section 6 case (c), a threat risk): the attacker needs physical access, a populated header and a protocol that by design accepts only read and reboot; 07 section 16.2 assesses L1. Level 1 (below 5 %), confidence Medium, until S2 and S3 are verified.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension performance_margin 4 by the regulatory rule of 06 section 7 (a changed calibration could breach 47 CFR 97.307); 07 section 16.2 scored C2 without that rule. Safety 2: the hardware PA-enable cutoff (HZ-004 K5) bounds a carrier.
risks.source: 07 section 16.2 row 'Diagnostic interface' (plan candidate SEP16-DIAG); opened 2026-09-25 after INSP-007 finding F-03

steps.action: Decide the diagnostic interface (UART header or USB CDC, populated or not on delivered units) in an ADR at PDR.
Write the SW-DIAG requirement that the protocol accepts only read commands and reboot (CS-33).
HostUnit injection cases showing that every other byte sequence on the interface has no effect on configuration or state (07 section 16.4).

triggers.condition: The PDR ADR adds a write command to the diagnostic protocol or populates the interface on delivered units
triggers.response: Claude re-assesses this risk the same session and adds the command to the S3 injection cases

triggers.condition: An S3 injection case fails
triggers.response: Claude opens an NCR the same session and blocks the release until the case passes

mitigation.fallback: Leave the diagnostic interface unpopulated on delivered units and read the event log from the display's diagnostic page only (07 section 16.5).

risks.closure_criteria: The S2 read-only requirement verified by the S3 injection cases on a credited HostUnit run, and the delivered-unit population recorded in the S1 ADR.

risks.title: Compromised toolchain or dependency inserts code into the image

statement.condition: 07 section 16.2 row 'Build and supply chain' assesses at L1, C4 the rustup-distributed toolchain, rustos, the development-tool crates and the vendored emulator; the planned controls are the toolchain from rustup with its signed manifests and an exact version pinned and hash-checked at accreditation, zero runtime crates (CS-02), cargo audit and cargo deny at every gate (SWE-185) and a reproducible-build check (MSR-28); no firmware release exists yet (firmware/releases/ is absent) and no accepted TV record exists for the Rust toolchain (docs/cm/tool-validation/ holds the 2026-09-25 evidence log rust-2026-09-25.log.txt only)
statement.departure: a compromised toolchain component or development dependency inserting code into the delivered firmware image
statement.asset: the SW image of the delivered units
statement.consequence: firmware behaviour that is not in the reviewed source, up to keying or emission outside the 47 CFR 97.305 or 97.307 limits or a defeated software safety check

risks.likelihood_rationale: Band argument (06 section 6 case (c), a threat risk): the image has zero runtime crates, rustos is owner-developed and reviewed under 07, the emulator never touches the image, and the remaining path is a compromise of the signed upstream toolchain distribution; 07 section 16.2 assesses L1. Level 1 (below 5 %), confidence Medium, until S1 and S2 run.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension performance_margin 4 by the regulatory rule of 06 section 7 (inserted code could breach 47 CFR 97.305 or 97.307); 07 section 16.2 scored C4. Safety 3: a defeated software thermal or charging check can destroy the unit, while the hardware interlocks (HZ-004 K5, HZ-002 controls) keep it below 4, as for RSK-020.
risks.source: 07 section 16.2 row 'Build and supply chain' (plan candidate SEP16-SUPPLY); RMM SWE-156 residual (OSS supply chain); opened 2026-09-25 after INSP-007 finding F-03

steps.action: Tool validation record of the Rust toolchain: exact version, manifest signature and hash recorded and checked (05 section 9.2).
cargo audit, cargo deny and the reproducible-build check run in the gate script on every gate, with results in the measurements file (SWE-185, MSR-28).
Every release VDD records the toolchain version and the image hash, verified on each delivered unit with picotool verify (PCA-05).

triggers.condition: cargo audit or cargo deny reports an advisory against a dependency or tool used in the build, or the reproducible-build check differs
triggers.response: Claude stops the release, opens an NCR the same session and re-assesses this risk

triggers.condition: A security advisory names the pinned toolchain version (trigger poll, 06 section 10.3)
triggers.response: Claude re-assesses this risk the same session and proposes a toolchain pin change to the owner by CR

mitigation.fallback: Rebuild from a clean, re-verified toolchain and reflash every unit from the re-verified release.

risks.closure_criteria: S1 TV record accepted by the owner, the S2 gate checks passing on the release built for SAR, and the S3 VDD hash verified on every delivered unit.

risks.title: Host mock diverges from RP2350 behaviour on a credited HostUnit case

statement.condition: charter section 9 makes HostUnit (application logic on the host implementation of the rustos api traits with injected device models) the primary software evidence (SI-026, ADR-011); ADR-011 section 4.4 proposes the risk 'host mock diverges from silicon behaviour' with contract tests against the mock and the dev board as its control, and 07 section 21 lists it; 07 section 19 makes a passing contract test against the mock and a filed dev-board check a closure condition of every work package; no contract test and no dev-board check exist yet
statement.departure: a behaviour credited by a HostUnit case differing on the RP2350 because the host mock of a rustos api trait does not model the silicon (register semantics, reset state, error returns or ordering)
statement.asset: the software verification evidence (HostUnit credit) and the firmware components of 07 section 14.1
statement.consequence: a requirement recorded Verified that fails on the delivered unit, found at Bench or on air, needing a firmware fix, a new tagged release and a credited re-run of the affected cases

risks.likelihood_rationale: Anchor level 4 (no analysis yet): no contract test compares any mock with the silicon, and a mock written from the same reading of the datasheet as the driver can share its misreading. 06 section 6 case (a) applies to this verification-fidelity risk as it does to RSK-003.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension schedule 3: a firmware fix, a new tagged release and a credited re-run of the affected cases is one design iteration (3 to 6 weeks). Safety 2: Bench confirmation of every hazard-tracing requirement on the delivered unit (07 section 9.7) stops a safety behaviour credited only on the mock from reaching use. First power-on 2: the fix is a firmware reflash.
risks.source: ADR-011 section 4.4 (candidate ADR011-R1, new risk proposed); 07 section 21 row 'Host mock diverges from silicon' (plan candidate SEP21-MOCK); opened 2026-09-25 after INSP-007 finding F-03

steps.action: Contract test suite per rustos api trait used by cwht, run against the host mock and on the Pico 2 dev board (Bench, credit false), as the work-package closure condition of 07 section 19 for the nine FW-B1 packages.
Mock fidelity statement per trait (what the mock models and what it does not), so that a HostUnit case cites only modelled behaviour.
Bench confirmation on the delivered unit of every hazard-tracing software requirement credited by HostUnit (07 section 9.7).
steps.artifact: docs/test_cases/sys/test_cases.json (Bench cases of the hazard-tracing requirements)

triggers.condition: A contract test passes on the mock and fails on the dev board, or a Bench case fails on a behaviour a HostUnit case credited
triggers.response: Claude opens an NCR the same session, withdraws the HostUnit credit of the affected cases and re-assesses this risk

triggers.condition: A rustos api trait changes (RSK-023)
triggers.response: Claude re-runs the S1 contract suite against the mock and the dev board before cwht moves to the new pinned commit

mitigation.fallback: Credit the affected requirements by Bench on the delivered unit only and restrict HostUnit credit to application logic that calls no mocked trait.

risks.closure_criteria: S1 contract suite passing on the mock and on the dev board for every trait cwht uses, and every hazard-tracing software requirement confirmed by Bench on the delivered unit (S3).

risks.title: Open or cold owner-soldered joint in a power path

statement.condition: under the kit model the owner hand-solders the through-hole parts and the modules with exposed pads, among them the Pico 2 castellations and the 18650 holders in the power path (charter section 12 row 'Assembly model', SI-031, ADR-007); ADR-007 section 4.4 proposes the risk 'owner-soldered joint defect in a power path', mitigated by the pre-power-on inspection; the controlled hand-assembly list is a CDR release item and does not exist yet
statement.departure: an open or high-resistance (cold) owner-soldered joint in a power path (cell holders, Pico 2 castellations, power switch or jack)
statement.asset: the PWR and CTL assemblies of the delivered units
statement.consequence: a unit that does not power or browns out under transmit load at first power-on until the owner finds and reworks the joint (a bridged joint at the cell holders is a short-circuit cause of HZ-007, carried by RSK-007)

risks.likelihood_rationale: Band argument (06 section 6 case (c), a workmanship risk that no design analysis bounds): the owner hand-solders the power-path joints of every unit (SI-031) and the pre-power-on inspection that ADR-007 names as the control is not yet written. Level 3 (20 % to 50 %), confidence Medium, until S1 exists.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension first_power_on 2: the fix is a hand rework of a part the owner solders (SI-031), with no PCB change. Safety 1: the open or cold joint removes power; the bridged-joint short is carried by RSK-007.
risks.source: ADR-007 section 4.4 (candidate ADR007-R1, new risk proposed); opened 2026-09-25 at the ADR candidate pass

steps.action: Bring-up stage 0: visual inspection and resistance check of every owner-soldered power-path joint, then a current-limited bench-supply power-up before cells are inserted.
Record the stage-0 result per unit in its as-built record.

triggers.condition: A stage-0 resistance or current-limit check fails on a unit
triggers.response: Owner reworks the joint; Claude records it in the unit's as-built record and re-assesses this risk before the next unit is powered

triggers.condition: The CDR hand-assembly list adds a power-path part
triggers.response: Claude re-assesses this risk the same session

mitigation.fallback: Move power-path parts to PCBWay assembly where a surface-mount alternate exists (kit-model change by CR).

risks.closure_criteria: Every delivered unit passes the stage-0 power-path check, with its result in docs/vv/adp/CWHT-A-NNN/as-built.md.

risks.title: Lending cwht units treated as outside the 15.23 personal-use exemption

statement.condition: 47 CFR 15.23(a) exempts from equipment authorization devices that are not marketed, are not constructed from a kit and are built in quantities of five or less for personal use (corpus: 47cfr-15.23.md, eCFR issue 2026-09-23); ADR-025 caps complete units at five across revisions (REQ-SYS-125, Draft), none marketed, kept by the owner and lent to friends (SI-035, SI-019); ADR-025 section 4.4 proposes the risk that the 'personal use' reading for lent units is Low confidence (docs/research/pcbway-export-and-vendor-questions.md F23)
statement.departure: the FCC, or a complaint to it, treating the lending of cwht units as outside the 15.23 personal-use exemption for the Part 15 digital section
statement.asset: the licensee's regulatory standing (SI-014) and the friend units (SI-019)
statement.consequence: units withdrawn from friends until the digital section is authorized or lending stops, so that the friend-unit input SI-019 is not met

risks.likelihood_rationale: Band argument (06 section 6 case (c), a regulatory-interpretation risk): the departure needs an inquiry or complaint about at most five unmarketed units operated by licensees. Level 1 (below 5 %); confidence Low because the reading itself is Low confidence in the research, so a re-assessment trigger is carried.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension performance_margin 4: a stakeholder input (SI-019, friend units) is not met (06 section 7 level 4). Cost 2: an authorization query or re-documentation.
risks.source: ADR-025 section 4.4 (candidate ADR025-R1, new risk proposed; also named in ADR-017 section 4.4); opened 2026-09-25 at the ADR candidate pass

steps.action: Owner decides whether to seek an FCC reading of lending under 15.23; Claude records the decision and any answer in an ADR.
Verify REQ-SYS-125 (at most five complete units, none marketed) by Inspection of the build records, with a lending record per unit.

triggers.condition: A unit is to be transferred, sold or offered to anyone, or more than five units are proposed
triggers.response: Claude re-assesses this risk the same session and the owner decides before the transfer or the order

triggers.condition: The FCC or anyone asks about a lent unit
triggers.response: Owner recalls the lent units pending the answer; Claude re-assesses this risk the same session

mitigation.fallback: Stop lending; friends operate units only with the owner present, or the owner seeks authorization of the digital section.

risks.closure_criteria: S1 decision recorded and REQ-SYS-125 verified by Inspection at SAR with the lending records of every unit.

Currency of the five 47 CFR 2.106 allocation rows
candidates.rationale: Same event family as REG-3 (a cited regulatory text changes unnoticed); its check is RSK-029 S2 (DECISION-10 browser check).

candidates.summary: Interpretation of third-party keying by a guest
candidates.rationale: Not a scored departure: the design supports either reading (guest lock FW-03, ADR-015), so an interpretation that limits third-party keying changes only the OPS-C text and the handbook, consequence 1 in every dimension. Re-open if an interpretation would require a firmware or hardware change.

candidates.rationale: RSK-025 (split from RSK-018 the same day) is this departure and carries HZ-009.

candidates.rationale: False keyer input from RF on the key lead is a cause of RSK-024 (HZ-010 K4 and K6 in steps S2 and S4); the audio thump on the headphone lead is a click cause bounded by the RSK-017 limiter and fade controls.

candidates.summary: Mono plug or stuck contact causes continuous transmission at power-on
candidates.rationale: A cause of RSK-024 (HZ-004 C-causes and the K1, K2 controls in step S1).

candidates.summary: Friends' keys may use mono plugs
candidates.rationale: A cause of RSK-024; the plug check and KEY CLOSED message are step S5 (HZ-004 K10).

candidates.summary: PWM audio noise and coupling
Earbuds up to 5 dB louder than the EN 50332-2 model
candidates.rationale: Same departure as RSK-017 (the level not bounded for the most sensitive earbud); RSK-017 S1 includes the 5 dB excess in the worst-case SPL.

candidates.summary: Pico 2 module USB current path unrated above 500 mA
Memory LCD unreadable in the dark
